title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation, and QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook documents the standard operating procedure for enterprise customer onboarding, integration validation, escalation handling, routine health checks, and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and relevant Engineering owners.

Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers (contracted Dedicated or Private deployments and larger Hosted customers > $5k/mo). Covers initial technical onboarding, post-integration verification, severity-based escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, ongoing health checks, and QBR artifacts.

Ownership and Roles

- Owner: Customer Success (CS) manager for the account (primary contact for non-technical coordination).
- Technical Lead: Assigned Solutions Engineer (SE) responsible for integration, API validation, and runbook handover.
- Support Pager: On-call SRE/Support engineer for production incidents.
- Engineering Escalation Lead: Responsible for bug triage and fix prioritization (runtime, routing, or infra teams).
- Product/Research: Involved for model-onboarding / quality regressions.

Service & Components Referenced

- api-gateway (authentication, rate limiting)
- inference-runtime (model serving, KV cache)
- routing-service (smart routing and fallbacks)
- telemetry-collector (events, token usage, latency histograms)
- console (dashboards, rollouts, alerts)

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (SE + CS)

1. Contract and SLAs: Verify the customer's contract template and SLA tiers (e.g., SLO: 99.9% monthly uptime; critical P1 response SLA: 1 hour).
2. Account Provisioning: Create org in Console, provision API keys, and set initial quotas.
3. Networking: Confirm VPC peering or private link requirements for Private deployments; confirm allowed IP ranges for Hosted.
4. IAM and KMS: Ensure KMS/HSM keys are configured for Private deployments if requested.
5. Sample Data/Prompts: Collect representative prompt sets and evals for quality verification and caching recommendations.
6. Telemetry: Ensure telemetry events are instrumented (request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, token_count, user_id).
7. Runbook Handover: Prepare the integration runbook, list of contacts, and escalation matrix.

Integration & Validation Guide (SE)

- Step 1: API Key & Sanity Test
  - Provide API key and example curl request. Validate: auth success, 200 OK, expected JSON schema.
  - Example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'

- Step 2: Traffic Pattern Simulation
  - Run load test representative of expected QPS (use locust or k6). Validate throughput, p95 latency, and token cost.
  - Target thresholds: p95 <= 350ms for Hosted-standard; p95 <= 200ms for Dedicated baseline (configurable per contract).

- Step 3: Model Pinning and Rollouts
  - Pin initial model variant (e.g., redwood/conv-v1-8b-quant). Document model_version in integration config.
  - Validate canary rollout: route 5% traffic to canary, monitor quality regressions for 48 hours.

- Step 4: Telemetry & Alerts
  - Ensure customer events appear in telemetry-collector within 60s. Configure alert rules in the console: errors > 1% over 10m, latency p95 above threshold for 5m.

Escalation Playbook (Severity-based)

Severity definitions (customer-facing):
- P1 / Critical: Production outage or total service unusable. Example: inference-runtime down for customer, returning 500s. Target: initial response within 1 hour; remediation/update every 30 minutes.
- P2 / High: Major degradation (high latency, large error rate impacting >= 25% of users). Target: initial response within 4 hours; remediation update every 4 hours.
- P3 / Medium: Partial impact or a functionality degradation with viable workaround. Target: initial response within 1 business day.
- P4 / Low: Cosmetic or enhancement requests. Target: initial response within 3 business days.

Escalation steps (P1 example)
1. Customer reports via support@redwood.ai or opens a ticket in Zendesk (priority set to P1).
2. Support on-call triages, assigns to SRE/Platform on-call, and posts to #incident-redwood (include org-id and request_id).
3. If not resolved within 30 minutes, escalate to Engineering Escalation Lead (page via PagerDuty).
4. SE and CS join customer bridge (Zoom) within 60 minutes for coordinated updates.
5. Post-incident: complete incident report and RCA within 72 hours.

Contact & Communication Channels

- Support portal: https://support.redwood.ai (Zendesk)
- Email: support@redwood.ai (enterprise routing)
- PagerDuty: onboarding team will receive escalation PD schedules; escalate through normal PD runbooks.
- Slack channels: #prod-ops (SRE), #cs-enterprise (CS and SE), #model-quality (Applied ML).

Support Process & Handover (Procedure)

- Step 1: Ticket Creation and Triage
  - All customer issues should be created in Zendesk with severity, affected components, and logs attached.
- Step 2: Initial Triage (Support)
  - Reproduce with provided request_id, collect request/response, and check console dashboards for errors and model health.
- Step 3: Assign to Owner
  - If root cause is: runtime bug -> assign to eng-serving-runtime; infra/networking -> eng-infra; quality/regression -> applied-ml-and-evals.
- Step 4: Resolution & Closure
  - Provide workaround if immediate fix is not available. Communicate expected ETA and update the ticket every status interval defined for severity.

Known Issues & Workarounds (Living List)

- Issue: Intermittent 429s during short bursts despite quota; Cause: conservative API-gateway token bucket limit.
  Workaround: Request temporary burst increase; configure client-side exponential backoff (initial retry 100ms, max 3 retries).
- Issue: Tokenization differences causing prompt length miscounts in embedded pipelines.
  Workaround: Use our token-encoder library (v1.2.0+) or truncate using our recommended safe window (reserve 64 tokens).
- Issue: Cold-start latency spikes for Private on-prem nodes after model swaps.
  Workaround: Pre-warm model variant with a synthetic traffic warmup script (recommended 5 requests / GPU).

Health Checks & QBR Materials

Recurring health-check cadence: weekly operational syncs + monthly health report + quarterly QBR.

Weekly (CS + SE):
- Review top 3 incidents, recent errors, and high-level usage trends.
- Validate canary results and rollout status.

Monthly:
- Produce a health report including: uptime (monthly), token usage and cost breakdown, top 10 endpoints by latency, and open support tickets.
- Include automated charts exported from console and a short narrative on performance trends.

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) Template
- Executive summary: key metrics (uptime, total tokens, average latency), wins, and top risks.
- Operational review: incidents since last QBR, availability trends, and remediation actions.
- Product & roadmap alignment: upcoming model upgrades, API changes, and feature requests.
- Cost optimization: batching, cache rules, and recommended quantization profiles with estimated unit-cost savings.
- Action items and owners: 3-5 prioritized work items, owners, and target dates.

Rollout & Handover Checklist (Post Integration)

- Deliverables to customer: integration runbook, monitoring playbook, and POC-to-prod checklist.
- Internal handover: transfer Jira epic, tag owners, and schedule recurring 1:1 CS/SE check-ins for 90 days.
- Close onboarding when: 1) 2 weeks of steady-state metrics within expected thresholds, 2) SE approves runbook, 3) CS and customer sign off.

Appendix: Contacts Matrix and Config Table

- Contacts: Provide names, roles, email, and PD escalation group (example row):
  - Aisha Patel, CS Lead, aisha.patel@redwood.ai, PD group: cs-leads-pd
  - Miguel Santos, SE Lead, miguel.santos@redwood.ai, PD group: se-leads-pd
  - On-call SRE, rotate@redwood.ai, PD group: platform-oncall

- Alert thresholds (example table in plain text):
  - Errors (5xx) > 1% over 10m -> Severity P2 -> Alert to #prod-ops and PagerDuty.
  - Latency p95 > configured threshold for 5m -> Severity P2 -> Alert to #prod-ops.
  - Telemetry missing for 60s -> Investigate telemetry-collector pipeline.

Appendix: Example Troubleshooting Commands

- Check recent failures for org: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <SE_API_TOKEN>" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/diagnostics/failures?org_id=<org>
- Tail inference-runtime logs (k8s): kubectl -n inference logs -l app=inference-runtime -f --tail=200

Document Maintenance

- Owners must review this playbook quarterly or after any major platform change (runtime release, routing policy update).
- Changes should be recorded in the page history with reviewer names and a short summary of changes.

Related pages and templates are listed in the metadata. For questions or to request customized onboarding templates, contact the CS manager assigned to the account.
